arxiv-2005-13976.title: Towards Automated Safety Coverage and Testing for Autonomous Vehicles with Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2005-13976.creator: Hyun Jae Cho, and Madhur Behl
arxiv-2005-13976.description: Abstract Abstract The kind of closed-loop verification likely to be required for autonomous vehicle (AV) safety testing is beyond the reach of traditional test methodologies and discrete verification. Validation puts the autonomous vehicle system to the test in scenarios or situations that the system would likely encounter in everyday driving after its release.

arxiv-2204-03714.title: Using Multiple Self-Supervised Tasks Improves Model Robustness
arxiv-2204-03714.creator: Matthew Lawhon, Chengzhi Mao & Junfeng Yang
arxiv-2204-03714.description: Abstract Deep networks achieve state-of-the-art performance on computer vision tasks, yet they fail under adversarial attacks that are imperceptible to humans. In this paper, we propose a novel defense that can dynamically adapt the input using the intrinsic structure from multiple self-supervised tasks.

arxiv-2408-15593.title: Skills Regularized Task Decomposition for Multi-task Offline Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2408-15593.creator: Minjong Yoo, Sangwoo Cho, Honguk Woo
arxiv-2408-15593.description: Abstract Reinforcement learning (RL) with diverse offline datasets can have the advantage of leveraging the relation of multiple tasks and the common skills learned across those tasks, hence allowing us to deal with real-world complex problems efficiently in a data-driven way.

arxiv-2409-14137.title: Triangulating on Possible Futures: Conducting User Studies on Several Futures Instead of Only One
arxiv-2409-14137.creator: Antti Salovaara, Leevi Vahvelainen
arxiv-2409-14137.description: Abstract . Plausible findings about futures are inherently difficult to obtain as they require critical, well-informed speculations backed with data. HCI scholars tackle this challenge via user studies wherein futuristic prototypes and other props concretise possible futures for participants. By observing participants’ actions, researchers then can ‘time travel’ to see that future as reality, in action.

arxiv-2410-15558.title: The effect of self-efficacy and pair programming experience in learning results of introductory programming courses
arxiv-2410-15558.creator: Yifan Mei Heng Ping Mingren Shen
arxiv-2410-15558.description: Abstract The purpose of this study was to explore the interactive effect of self-efficacy and pair programming experience to the final learning results in introductory programming courses. We developed a 2x2 fractional design to explore their roles and relationships. Data was collected by distributing questionnaires to students have learnt or are learning CS367 at UW-Madison.

arxiv-2501-09871.title: Generalized Doubly Parabolic Keller-Segel System with Fractional Diffusion
arxiv-2501-09871.creator: Anne Bronzi 1 and Crystianne De Andrade 2
arxiv-2501-09871.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Anne Bronzi 1 and Crystianne De Andrade 2. The Keller-Segel model is a system of partial differential equations that describes the movement of cells or organisms in response to chemical signals, a phenomenon known as chemotaxis. In this study, we analyze a doubly parabolic Keller-Segel system in the whole space ℝ d \mathbb{R}^{d} , d ≥ 2 d\geq 2 , where both cellular and chemical diffusion are governed by fractional Laplacians with distinct exponents.

arxiv-2501-10635.title: Quasi-linear maps and image transformations
arxiv-2501-10635.creator: S. V. Butler
arxiv-2501-10635.description: Abstract . Conic quasi-linear maps are nonlinear operators from C 0 ​ ( X ) C_{0}(X) to a normed linear space E E which preserve nonnegative linear combinations on positive cones generated by single functions; quasi-linear maps are linear on singly generated subalgebras. While nonlinear, a quasi-linear map is bounded iff it is continuous.

pmc-10672798.title: The Role of Immune Cells in the Pathogenesis of Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis
pmc-10672798.creator: Yahan Xu, Peixiang Lan, Tao Wang
pmc-10672798.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a devastating disease of unknown etiology with limited treatment options. The role of the immune system in IPF has received increasing attention. Uncontrolled immune responses drive the onset and progression of IPF.

pmc-11477581.title: Selecting a Brief Cognitive Screening Test Based on Patient Profile: It Is Never Too Early to Start
pmc-11477581.creator: Gemma García-Lluch, Ariadna Muedra-Moreno, Mar García-Zamora, Beatriz Gómez, Rafael Sánchez-Roy, Lucrecia Moreno, Mohamad El Haj
pmc-11477581.description: Introduction: Cognitive impairment, marked by a decline in memory and attention, is frequently underdiagnosed, complicating effective management. Cardiovascular risk factors (CVR) and anticholinergic burden (ACB) are significant contributors to dementia risk, with ACB often stemming from medications prescribed for neuropsychiatric disorders. This study evaluates cognitive profiles through three brief cognitive tests, analyzing the impact of CVR and ACB presence.

pmc-11525574.title: Application of artistic design innovation in promoting rural cultural brand construction
pmc-11525574.creator: Min Zeng, Chao Jin
pmc-11525574.description: To conduct an in-depth analysis of global users’ emotional and aesthetic preferences for rural cultural brands and to accurately assess the varying popularity of different design elements across countries, this study utilizes the EmoRuralSim simulator in combination with artificial intelligence and text mining techniques.

pmc-11612432.title: Semantic segmentation network for mangrove tree species based on UAV remote sensing images
pmc-11612432.creator: Xin Wang, Yu Zhang, Jingye Ca, Qin Qin, Yi Feng, Jingke Yan
pmc-11612432.description: Mangroves are special vegetation that grows in the intertidal zone of the coast and has extremely high ecological and environmental value. Different mangrove species exhibit significant differences in ecological functions and environmental responses, so accurately identifying and distinguishing these species is crucial for ecological protection and monitoring.

pmc-12591093.title: Dysregulation of astrocyte-secreted pleiotrophin contributes to neuronal structural and functional deficits in Down syndrome
pmc-12591093.creator: Ashley N Brandebura, Adrien Paumier, Quinn N Asbell, Tao Tao, Mariel Kristine B Micael, Sherlyn Sanchez, Nicola J Allen
pmc-12591093.description: SUMMARYNeuronal dendrite patterning and synapse formation are tightly regulated during development to promote proper connectivity. Here, we identify downregulation of pleiotrophin, a secreted molecule enriched in astrocytes, as a major contributor to dendrite and synapse deficits in the Ts65Dn mouse model of Down syndrome (DS).

pmc-12683486.title: Circulating stem-like exhausted CD8 T cells point to better outcomes in lung cancer: a brief report
pmc-12683486.creator: Linda Ye, Ian Dick, Tina Firth, Bruce W. Robinson, Jenette Creaney, Alec Redwood
pmc-12683486.description: Anti-cancer T cells exhibit a spectrum of functional abilities and exhaustion levels and can be broadly categorized as stem-like exhausted T cells (Texstem) that retain cancer-killing capacity, and terminally exhausted T cells (Texterm) with limited function. Previously, we identified CD8 Texstem and Texterm cells in malignant pleural effusions (PEs) of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and mesothelioma patients.

pmc-12722743.title: Enhanced production of active species and NH3 using non-equilibrium ferroelectric barrier discharge
pmc-12722743.creator: Yijie Xu, Ziqiao Chang, Zhiyu Shi, Zijian Sun, Henrik Burda, Weixiao Wang, Ning Liu, Yiguang Ju
pmc-12722743.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Non-equilibrium plasma-assisted ammonia synthesis is investigated through enhanced active species production with ferroelectric discharge. Time-resolved in-situ diagnostics of femtosecond two-photon absorption laser-induced fluorescence, coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering, and laser absorption spectroscopy, as well as optical emission spectroscopy, were conducted to probe the key intermediate species, such as H and N radicals as well as N2(ν), ions, and NH3 to achieve better understanding of non-equilibrium energy transfer and ammonia formation. The results reveal that ferroelectric discharge improved ammonia yield by four times.

pmc-13491301.title: The richness, frequency and relatedness components of mate diversity and mate portfolios
pmc-13491301.creator: Lawrence D. Harder, Mason W. Kulbaba
pmc-13491301.description: Summary Sexual reproduction produces genetically diverse families, especially when individuals mate with multiple partners.During mating, an individual accumulates a mate portfolio, the diversity of which depends on the number of mates, their relative mating contributions and characteristics. Nevertheless, studies of mate diversity generally focus on mate number or correlated mating, the probability that pairs of offspring are full siblings.
